text:
Situation: FDA first posted the hydromorphone hydrochloride shortage on 2017-10-31 and it remains current as of 2026-10-21. Our injection supply (NDC 00409128331) is labeled by Hospira, Inc. from plants FEI 1021343 and FEI 1925262. Corvale East holds 304 units of 1 mg/mL 1 mL cartridges (17.5 days) and 58 units of 2 mg/mL 20 mL SDV (2.8 days). Corvale General holds three lots totaling 1,223 units (13.8–29.1 days each).

Why (FDA record): FDA inspection 976095 at FEI 1925262 ended 2016-06-08 and was classified OAI, 510 days before the shortage posting. A Warning Letter was issued to FEI 1925262 on 2017-02-14, 259 days before the shortage posting. FDA inspection 1064827 at FEI 1925262 ended 2018-08-15 and was classified OAI, with the classification letter dated 2020-04-22.

Our position: Corvale East is critically low on the 2 mg/mL 20 mL SDV (2.8 days). Corvale General has sufficient aggregate supply to support a transfer without dropping below two weeks on hand.

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 173 units from Corvale General to Corvale East — approved by pharmacy director (transfer request).
2. Use HYDROmorphone Hydrochloride 2 mg/mL from Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA Inc. — recalculate dose and volume; pharmacist verification required; approved by Sam Rivera, MD on 2025-10-13.
3. Use HYDROmorphone HYDROCHLORIDE 1 mg/mL from Hospira, Inc. — recalculate dose and volume; pharmacist verification required; approved by Sam Rivera, MD on 2026-06-05.

Not recommended: Delaying transfer or substitution while Corvale East 2 mg/mL 20 mL SDV remains below three days on hand.
